name: RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge
description: In this work, we describe our approach to pneumonia classification and localization in chest radiographs. This method uses only \emph{open-source} deep learning object detection and is based on CoupleNet, a fully convolutional network which incorporates global and local features for object detection. Our approach achieves robustness through critical modifications of the training process and a novel ensembling algorithm which merges bounding boxes from several models. We tested our detection algorithm tested on a dataset of 3000 chest radiographs as part of the 2018 RSNA Pneumonia Challenge; our solution was recognized as a winning entry in a contest which attracted more than 1400 participants worldwide.
evaluation_method: mean average precision over bounding-box detections
typical_sota_score: commonly reported strong solutions achieve high detection AP on the private leaderboard, but scores vary substantially with thresholding and post-processing
notes: This benchmark is sensitive to annotation noise and the ambiguity of pneumonia appearance on X-rays. Solutions often use object detection architectures with heavy augmentation and ensembles.
